24837.text: “Tell us, When will these things be, and what will be the sign when all these things are destined to come to a conclusion?”

24838.label: Mark 13:5
24838.text: So Jesus started to say to them: “Look out that nobody misleads YOU.

24839.label: Mark 13:6
24839.text: Many will come on the basis of my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and will mislead many.

24840.label: Mark 13:7
24840.text: Moreover, when YOU hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be terrified; [these things] must take place, but the end is not yet.

24841.label: Mark 13:8
24841.text: “For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, there will be earthquakes in one place after another, there will be food shortages. These are a beginning of pangs of distress.

24842.label: Mark 13:9
24842.text: “As for YOU, look out for yourselves; people will deliver YOU up to local courts, and YOU will be beaten in synagogues and be put on the stand before governors and kings for my sake, for a witness to them.

24843.label: Mark 13:10
24843.text: Also, in all the nations the good news has to be preached first.

24844.label: Mark 13:11
24844.text: But when they are leading YOU along to deliver YOU up, do not be anxious beforehand about what to speak; but whatever is given YOU in that hour, speak this, for YOU are not the ones speaking, but the holy spirit is.

24845.label: Mark 13:12
24845.text: Furthermore, brother will deliver brother over to death, and a father a child, and children will rise up against parents and have them put to death;

24846.label: Mark 13:13
24846.text: and YOU will be objects of hatred by all people on account of my name. But he that has endured to the end is the one that will be saved.

24847.label: Mark 13:14
24847.text: “However, when YOU catch sight of the disgusting thing that causes desolation standing where it ought not (let the reader use discernment), then let those in Ju·deʹa begin fleeing to the mountains.

24848.label: Mark 13:15
24848.text: Let the man on the housetop not come down, nor go inside to take anything out of his house;

24849.label: Mark 13:16
24849.text: and let the man in the field not return to the things behind to pick up his outer garment.

24850.label: Mark 13:17
24850.text: Woe to the pregnant women and those suckling a baby in those days!

24851.label: Mark 13:18
24851.text: Keep praying that it may not occur in wintertime;

24852.label: Mark 13:19
24852.text: for those days will be [days of] a tribulation such as has not occurred from [the] beginning of the creation which God created until that time, and will not occur again.

24853.label: Mark 13:20
24853.text: In fact, unless Jehovah had cut short the days, no flesh would be saved. But on account of the chosen ones whom he has chosen he has cut short the days.

24854.label: Mark 13:21
24854.text: “Then, too, if anyone says to YOU, ‘See! Here is the Christ,’ ‘See! There he is,’ do not believe [it].

24855.label: Mark 13:22
24855.text: For false Christs and false prophets will arise and will give signs and wonders to lead astray, if possible, the chosen ones.

24856.label: Mark 13:23
24856.text: YOU, then, watch out; I have told YOU all things beforehand.

24857.label: Mark 13:24
24857.text: “But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light,

24858.label: Mark 13:25
24858.text: and the stars will be falling out of heaven, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.

24859.label: Mark 13:26
24859.text: And then they will see the Son of man coming in clouds with great power and glory.

24860.label: Mark 13:27
24860.text: And then he will send forth the angels and will gather his chosen ones together from the four winds, from earth’s extremity to heaven’s extremity.

24861.label: Mark 13:28
24861.text: “Now from the fig tree learn the illustration: Just as soon as its young branch grows tender and puts forth its leaves, YOU know that summer is near.

24862.label: Mark 13:29
24862.text: Likewise also YOU, when YOU see these things happening, know that he is near, at the doors.

24863.label: Mark 13:30
24863.text: Truly I say to YOU that this generation will by no means pass away until all these things happen.

24864.label: Mark 13:31
24864.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.

24865.label: Mark 13:32
24865.text: “Concerning that day or the hour nobody knows, neither the angels in heaven nor the Son, but the Father.

24866.label: Mark 13:33
24866.text: Keep looking, keep awake, for YOU do not know when the appointed time is.

24867.label: Mark 13:34
24867.text: It is like a man traveling abroad that left his house and gave the authority to his slaves, to each one his work, and commanded the doorkeeper to keep on the watch.

24868.label: Mark 13:35
24868.text: Therefore keep on the watch, for YOU do not know when the master of the house is coming, whether late in the day or at midnight or at cockcrowing or early in the morning;

24869.label: Mark 13:36
24869.text: in order that when he arrives suddenly, he does not find YOU sleeping.

24870.label: Mark 13:37
24870.text: But what I say to YOU I say to all, Keep on the watch.”

24871.label: Mark 14:1
24871.text: Now the passover and the [festival of] unfermented cakes was two days later. And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how to seize him by crafty device and kill him;

24872.label: Mark 14:2
24872.text: for they repeatedly said: “Not at the festival; perhaps there might be an uproar of the people.”

24873.label: Mark 14:3
24873.text: And while he was at Bethʹa·ny in the house of Simon the leper, as he was reclining at the meal, a woman came with an alabaster case of perfumed oil, genuine nard, very expensive. Breaking open the alabaster case she began to pour it upon his head.

24874.label: Mark 14:4
24874.text: At this there were some expressing indignation among themselves: “Why has this waste of the perfumed oil taken place?

24875.label: Mark 14:5
24875.text: For this perfumed oil could have been sold for upward of three hundred de·narʹi·i and been given to the poor!” And they were feeling great displeasure at her.

24876.label: Mark 14:6
24876.text: But Jesus said: “Let her alone. Why do YOU try to make trouble for her? She did a fine deed toward me.

24877.label: Mark 14:7
24877.text: For YOU always have the poor with YOU, and whenever YOU want to YOU can always do them good, but me YOU do not have always.

24878.label: Mark 14:8
24878.text: She did what she could; she undertook beforehand to put perfumed oil on my body in view of the burial.

24879.label: Mark 14:9
24879.text: Truly I say to YOU, Wherever the good news is preached in all the world, what this woman did shall also be told as a remembrance of her.”

24880.label: Mark 14:10
24880.text: And Judas Is·carʹi·ot, one of the twelve, went off to the chief priests in order to betray him to them.

24881.label: Mark 14:11
24881.text: When they heard it, they rejoiced and promised to give him silver money. So he began seeking how to betray him conveniently.

24882.label: Mark 14:12
24882.text: Now on the first day of unfermented cakes, when they customarily sacrificed the passover [victim], his disciples said to him: “Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the passover?”

24883.label: Mark 14:13
24883.text: With that he sent forth two of his disciples and said to them: “Go into the city, and a man carrying an earthenware vessel of water will encounter YOU. Follow him,

24884.label: Mark 14:14
24884.text: and wherever he goes inside say to the householder, ‘The Teacher says: “Where is the guest room for me where I may eat the passover with my disciples?”’

24885.label: Mark 14:15
24885.text: And he will show YOU a large upper room, furnished in preparation; and there prepare for us.”

24886.label: Mark 14:16
24886.text: So the disciples went out, and they entered the city and found it just as he said to them; and they prepared for the passover.

24887.label: Mark 14:17
24887.text: After evening had fallen he came with the twelve.

24888.label: Mark 14:18
24888.text: And as they were reclining at the table and eating, Jesus said: “Truly I say to YOU, One of YOU, who is eating with me, will betray me.”

24889.label: Mark 14:19
24889.text: They started to be grieved and to say to him one by one: “It is not I, is it?”

24890.label: Mark 14:20
24890.text: He said to them: “It is one of the twelve, who is dipping with me into the common bowl.

24891.label: Mark 14:21
24891.text: True, the Son of man is going away, just as it is written concerning him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of man is betrayed! It would have been finer for that man if he had not been born.”

24892.label: Mark 14:22
24892.text: And as they continued eating, he took a loaf, said a blessing, broke it and gave it to them, and said: “Take it, this means my body.”

24893.label: Mark 14:23
24893.text: And taking a cup, he offered thanks and gave it to them, and they all drank out of it.

24894.label: Mark 14:24
24894.text: And he said to them: “This means my ‘blood of the covenant,’ which is to be poured out in behalf of many.

24895.label: Mark 14:25
24895.text: Truly I say to YOU, I shall by no means drink anymore of the product of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”

24896.label: Mark 14:26
24896.text: Finally, after singing praises, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

24897.label: Mark 14:27
24897.text: And Jesus said to them: “YOU will all be stumbled, because it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered about.’

24898.label: Mark 14:28
24898.text: But after I have been raised up I will go ahead of YOU into Galʹi·lee.”

24899.label: Mark 14:29
24899.text: But Peter said to him: “Even if all the others are stumbled, yet I will not be.”

24900.label: Mark 14:30
24900.text: At that Jesus said to him: “Truly I say to you, You today, yes, this night, before a cock crows twice, even you will disown me three times.”

24901.label: Mark 14:31
24901.text: But he began to say profusely: “If I have to die with you, I will by no means disown you.” Also, all the others began saying the same thing.

24902.label: Mark 14:32
24902.text: So they came to a spot named Geth·semʹa·ne, and he said to his disciples: “Sit down here while I pray.”

24903.label: Mark 14:33
24903.text: And he took Peter and James and John along with him, and he started to be stunned and to be sorely troubled.

24904.label: Mark 14:34
24904.text: And he said to them: “My soul is deeply grieved, even to death. Stay here and keep on the watch.”

24905.label: Mark 14:35
24905.text: And going a little way forward he proceeded to fall on the ground and began praying that, if it were possible, the hour might pass away from him.

24906.label: Mark 14:36
24906.text: And he went on to say: “Abba, Father, all things are possible to you; remove this cup from me. Yet not what I want, but what you want.”

24907.label: Mark 14:37
24907.text: And he came and found them sleeping, and he said to Peter: “Simon, are you sleeping? Did you not have strength to keep on the watch one hour?

24908.label: Mark 14:38
24908.text: Men, keep on the watch and praying, in order that YOU do not come into temptation. The spirit, of course, is eager, but the flesh is weak.”

24909.label: Mark 14:39
24909.text: And he went away again and prayed, saying the same word.

24910.label: Mark 14:40
24910.text: And again he came and found them sleeping, for their eyes were weighed down, and so they did not know what to answer him.

24911.label: Mark 14:41
24911.text: And he came the third time and said to them: “At such a time as this YOU are sleeping and taking YOUR rest! It is enough! The hour has come! Look! The Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

24912.label: Mark 14:42
24912.text: Get up, let us go. Look! My betrayer has drawn near.”

24913.label: Mark 14:43
24913.text: And immediately, while he was yet speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived and with him a crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests and the scribes and the older men.

24914.label: Mark 14:44
24914.text: Now his betrayer had given them an agreed sign, saying: “Whoever it is I kiss, this is he; take him into custody and lead him away safely.”

24915.label: Mark 14:45
24915.text: And he came straight up and approached him and said: “Rabbi!” and kissed him very tenderly.

24916.label: Mark 14:46
24916.text: So they laid their hands upon him and took him into custody.

24917.label: Mark 14:47
24917.text: However, a certain one of those standing by drew his sword and struck the slave of the high priest and took his ear off.

24918.label: Mark 14:48
24918.text: But in response Jesus said to them: “Did YOU come out with swords and clubs as against a robber to arrest me?

24919.label: Mark 14:49
24919.text: Day after day I was with YOU in the temple teaching, and yet YOU did not take me into custody. Nevertheless, it is in order that the Scriptures may be fulfilled.”

24920.label: Mark 14:50
24920.text: And they all abandoned him and fled.

24921.label: Mark 14:51
24921.text: But a certain young man wearing a fine linen garment over his naked body began to follow him nearby; and they tried to seize him,

24922.label: Mark 14:52
24922.text: but he left his linen garment behind and got away naked.

24923.label: Mark 14:53
24923.text: They now led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests and the older men and the scribes assembled.

24924.label: Mark 14:54
24924.text: But Peter, from a good distance, followed him as far as in the courtyard of the high priest; and he was sitting together with the house attendants and warming himself before a bright fire.

24925.label: Mark 14:55
24925.text: Meantime the chief priests and the whole Sanʹhe·drin were looking for testimony against Jesus to put him to death, but they were not finding any.

24926.label: Mark 14:56
24926.text: Many, indeed, were giving false witness against him, but their testimonies were not in agreement.

24927.label: Mark 14:57
24927.text: Also, certain ones were rising and bearing false witness against him, saying:

24928.label: Mark 14:58
24928.text: “We heard him say, ‘I will throw down this temple that was made with hands and in three days I will build another not made with hands.’”

24929.label: Mark 14:59
24929.text: But neither on these grounds was their testimony in agreement.

24930.label: Mark 14:60
24930.text: Finally the high priest rose in their midst and questioned Jesus, saying: “Do you say nothing in reply? What is it these are testifying against you?”

24931.label: Mark 14:61
24931.text: But he kept silent and made no reply at all. Again the high priest began to question him and said to him: “Are you the Christ the Son of the Blessed One?”

24932.label: Mark 14:62
24932.text: Then Jesus said: “I am; and YOU persons will see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”

24933.label: Mark 14:63
24933.text: At this the high priest ripped his inner garments and said: “What further need do we have of witnesses?

24934.label: Mark 14:64
24934.text: YOU heard the blasphemy. What is evident to YOU?” They all condemned him to be liable to death.

24935.label: Mark 14:65
24935.text: And some started to spit on him and to cover his whole face and hit him with their fists and say to him: “Prophesy!” And, slapping him in the face, the court attendants took him.

24936.label: Mark 14:66
24936.text: Now while Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the servant girls of the high priest came,

24937.label: Mark 14:67
24937.text: and, seeing Peter warming himself, she looked straight at him and said: “You, too, were with the Naz·a·reneʹ, this Jesus.”

24938.label: Mark 14:68
24938.text: But he denied it, saying: “Neither do I know him nor do I understand what you are saying,” and he went outside to the vestibule.

24939.label: Mark 14:69
24939.text: There the servant girl, at the sight of him, started again to say to those standing by: “This is one of them.”

24940.label: Mark 14:70
24940.text: Again he was denying it. And once more after a little while those standing by began saying to Peter: “Certainly you are one of them, for, in fact, you are a Gal·i·leʹan.”

24941.label: Mark 14:71
24941.text: But he commenced to curse and swear: “I do not know this man of whom YOU speak.”

24942.label: Mark 14:72
24942.text: And immediately a cock crowed a second time; and Peter recalled the saying that Jesus spoke to him: “Before a cock crows twice, you will disown me three times.” And he broke down and gave way to weeping.

24943.label: Mark 15:1
24943.text: And immediately at dawn the chief priests with the older men and the scribes, even the whole Sanʹhe·drin, conducted a consultation, and they bound Jesus and led him off and handed him over to Pilate.

24944.label: Mark 15:2
24944.text: So Pilate put the question to him: “Are you the king of the Jews?” In answer to him he said: “You yourself say [it].”

24945.label: Mark 15:3
24945.text: But the chief priests proceeded to accuse him of many things.

24946.label: Mark 15:4
24946.text: Now Pilate began questioning him again, saying: “Have you no reply to make? See how many charges they are bringing against you.”

24947.label: Mark 15:5
24947.text: But Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate began to marvel.

24948.label: Mark 15:6
24948.text: Well, from festival to festival he used to release to them one prisoner, whom they petitioned for.

24949.label: Mark 15:7
24949.text: At the time there was the so-called Bar·abʹbas in bonds with the seditionists, who in their sedition had committed murder.

24950.label: Mark 15:8
24950.text: So the crowd came on up and started to make petition according to what he used to do for them.

24951.label: Mark 15:9
24951.text: Pilate responded to them, saying: “Do YOU want me to release to YOU the king of the Jews?”

24952.label: Mark 15:10
24952.text: For he was aware that because of envy the chief priests had handed him over.

24953.label: Mark 15:11
24953.text: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Bar·abʹbas to them, instead.

24954.label: Mark 15:12
24954.text: Again in reply Pilate was saying to them: “What, then, shall I do with him whom YOU call the king of the Jews?”

24955.label: Mark 15:13
24955.text: Once more they cried out: “Impale him!”

24956.label: Mark 15:14
24956.text: But Pilate went on to say to them: “Why, what bad thing did he do?” Still they cried out all the more: “Impale him!”

24957.label: Mark 15:15
24957.text: At that Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd, released Bar·abʹbas to them, and, after having Jesus whipped, he handed him over to be impaled.

24958.label: Mark 15:16
24958.text: The soldiers now led him off into the courtyard, that is, into the governor’s palace; and they called the whole body of troops together,

24959.label: Mark 15:17
24959.text: and they decked him with purple and braided a crown of thorns and put it on him.

24960.label: Mark 15:18
24960.text: And they started greeting him: “Good day, you King of the Jews!”

24961.label: Mark 15:19
24961.text: Also, they would hit him on the head with a reed and spit upon him and, bending their knees, they would do obeisance to him.

24962.label: Mark 15:20
24962.text: Finally, when they had made fun of him, they stripped him of the purple and put his outer garments upon him. And they led him out to impale him.

24963.label: Mark 15:21
24963.text: Also, they impressed into service a passerby, a certain Simon of Cy·reʹne, coming from the country, the father of Alexander and Ruʹfus, that he should lift up his torture stake.

24964.label: Mark 15:22
24964.text: So they brought him to the place Golʹgo·tha, which means, when translated, Skull Place.

24965.label: Mark 15:23
24965.text: Here they tried to give him wine drugged with myrrh, but he would not take it.

24966.label: Mark 15:24
24966.text: And they impaled him and distributed his outer garments by casting the lot over them as to who takes what.

24967.label: Mark 15:25
24967.text: It was now the third hour, and they impaled him.

24968.label: Mark 15:26
24968.text: And the inscription of the charge against him was written above, “The King of the Jews.”

24969.label: Mark 15:27
24969.text: Moreover, they impaled two robbers with him, one on his right and one on his left.

24971.label: Mark 15:29
24971.text: And those going by would speak abusively to him, wagging their heads and saying: “Bah! You would-be thrower-down of the temple and builder of it in three days’ time,

24972.label: Mark 15:30
24972.text: save yourself by coming down off the torture stake.”

24973.label: Mark 15:31
24973.text: In like manner also the chief priests were making fun among themselves with the scribes and saying: “Others he saved; himself he cannot save!

24974.label: Mark 15:32
24974.text: Let the Christ the King of Israel now come down off the torture stake, that we may see and believe.” Even those impaled together with him were reproaching him.

24975.label: Mark 15:33
24975.text: When it became the sixth hour a darkness fell over the whole land until the ninth hour.

24976.label: Mark 15:34
24976.text: And at the ninth hour Jesus called out with a loud voice: “Eʹli, Eʹli, laʹma sa·bach·thaʹni?” which means, when translated: “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”

24977.label: Mark 15:35
24977.text: And some of those standing near, on hearing it, began to say: “See! He is calling E·liʹjah.”

24978.label: Mark 15:36
24978.text: But a certain one ran, soaked a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed, and began giving him a drink, saying: “LET [him] be! Let us see whether E·liʹjah comes to take him down.”

24979.label: Mark 15:37
24979.text: But Jesus let out a loud cry and expired.

24980.label: Mark 15:38
24980.text: And the curtain of the sanctuary was rent in two from top to bottom.

24981.label: Mark 15:39
24981.text: Now, when the army officer that was standing by with him in view saw he had expired under these circumstances, he said: “Certainly this man was God’s Son.”

24982.label: Mark 15:40
24982.text: There were also women viewing from a distance, among them Mary Magʹda·lene as well as Mary the mother of James the Less and of Joʹses, and Sa·loʹme,

24983.label: Mark 15:41
24983.text: who used to accompany him and minister to him when he was in Galʹi·lee, and many other women who had come up together with him to Jerusalem.

24984.label: Mark 15:42
24984.text: Now as it was already late in the afternoon, and since it was Preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath,

24985.label: Mark 15:43
24985.text: there came Joseph of Ar·i·ma·theʹa, a reputable member of the Council, who also himself was waiting for the kingdom of God. He took courage to go in before Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

24986.label: Mark 15:44
24986.text: But Pilate wondered whether he was already dead, and, summoning the army officer, he asked him whether he had already died.

24987.label: Mark 15:45
24987.text: So after making certain from the army officer, he granted the corpse to Joseph.

24988.label: Mark 15:46
24988.text: Accordingly he bought fine linen and took him down, wrapped him in the fine linen and laid him in a tomb which was quarried out of a rock-mass; and he rolled a stone up to the door of the memorial tomb.

24989.label: Mark 15:47
24989.text: But Mary Magʹda·lene and Mary the mother of Joʹses continued looking at where he had been laid.

24990.label: Mark 16:1
24990.text: So when the sabbath had passed, Mary Magʹda·lene, and Mary the mother of James, and Sa·loʹme bought spices in order to come and grease him.

24991.label: Mark 16:2
24991.text: And very early on the first day of the week they came to the memorial tomb, when the sun had risen.

24992.label: Mark 16:3
24992.text: And they were saying one to another: “Who will roll the stone away from the door of the memorial tomb for us?”

24993.label: Mark 16:4
24993.text: But when they looked up, they beheld that the stone had been rolled away, although it was very large.

24994.label: Mark 16:5
24994.text: When they entered into the memorial tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side clothed in a white robe, and they were stunned.

24995.label: Mark 16:6
24995.text: He said to them: “Stop being stunned. YOU are looking for Jesus the Naz·a·reneʹ, who was impaled. He was raised up, he is not here. See! The place where they laid him.

24996.label: Mark 16:7
24996.text: But go, tell his disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of YOU into Galʹi·lee; there YOU will see him, just as he told YOU.’”

24997.label: Mark 16:8
24997.text: So when they came out they fled from the memorial tomb, for trembling and strong emotion were gripping them. And they told nobody anything, for they were in fear. SHORT CONCLUSION Some late manuscripts and versions contain a short conclusion after Mark 16:8, as follows: But all the things that had been commanded they related briefly to those around Peter. Further, after these things, Jesus himself sent out through them from the east to the west the holy and incorruptible proclamation of everlasting salvation.

24998.label: Mark 16:9
24998.text: After he rose early on the first day of the week he appeared first to Mary Magʹda·lene, from whom he had expelled seven demons.

24999.label: Mark 16:10
24999.text: She went and reported to those who had been with him, as they were mourning and weeping.

25000.label: Mark 16:11
25000.text: But they, when they heard he had come to life and had been viewed by her, did not believe.

25001.label: Mark 16:12
25001.text: Moreover, after these things he appeared in another form to two of them walking along, as they were going into the country;

25002.label: Mark 16:13
25002.text: and they came back and reported to the rest. Neither did they believe these.

25003.label: Mark 16:14
25003.text: But later he appeared to the eleven themselves as they were reclining at the table, and he reproached their lack of faith and hardheartedness, because they did not believe those who had beheld him now raised up from the dead.

25004.label: Mark 16:15
25004.text: And he said to them: “Go into all the world and preach the good news to all creation.

25005.label: Mark 16:16
25005.text: He that believes and is baptized will be saved, but he that does not believe will be condemned.

25006.label: Mark 16:17
25006.text: Furthermore, these signs will accompany those believing: By the use of my name they will expel demons, they will speak with tongues,

25007.label: Mark 16:18
25007.text: and with their hands they will pick up serpents, and if they drink anything deadly it will not hurt them at all. They will lay their hands upon sick persons, and these will become well.”

25008.label: Mark 16:19
25008.text: So, then, the Lord Jesus, after having spoken to them, was taken up to heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.

25009.label: Mark 16:20
25009.text: They, accordingly, went out and preached everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and backed up the message through the accompanying signs.
